Mocha is part of 5 of my public repositories, from 2013 to 2025.

What it was for: [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (2), [Learning and experiments](@/projects/learning.md) (1), [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (1) and [Web](@/projects/web.md) (1).

Most recently: [microcrawler-browser](@/work/microcrawler-browser.md): Proof-of-Concept: Microcrawler in your Browser!; [apollocrawler.com](@/work/apollocrawler-com.md): Website for apollocrawler.com; [craftsmen](@/work/craftsmen.md): Web UI for listing of czech companies.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses Mocha: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links Mocha to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
